pathway.title: Kaiser Aluminum Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Deleveraging is real and mostly earnings-driven: net debt of USD 921.4 million (USD 934.2 million pro forma for the dividend) is 1.98x trailing EBITDA (2.00x pro forma) against 3.38x at 2025-12-31, a fall of 1.40x of which 1.12x came from higher EBITDA and only 0.28x from lower net debt. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-1

Underlying earnings improved by more than the metal price lag explains: Adjusted EBITDA excluding the favorable lag was USD 315.8 million in the nine months of 2026 against USD 158.4 million a year earlier, and the lag's share of Adjusted EBITDA fell from 28.78% to 16.63%. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation CALC-2

Momentum is slowing and the trailing figures flatter the run rate: Adjusted EBITDA fell from an average of USD 147.4 million a quarter in the first half to USD 84.0 million in the third quarter, and the outlook, which the issuer now places toward the low end of 45% to 55% growth, implies about USD 70.99 million in the fourth quarter if it lands at 45%, which puts leverage at 2.97x on the second-half run rate before the dividend. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 31; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4

Free cash flow is the least proven dimension: it was USD -13.7 million in FY2024 and USD -25.5 million in FY2025 and reached USD 124.8 million on a trailing basis only after capital spending fell and USD 157.2 million of payables built, so cash conversion has not been shown through a metal price cycle. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-20

Business risk is moderate and customer-led: packaging is 39.95% and aerospace plate 31.00% of nine-month 2026 conversion revenue, but the two largest customers take 31% of net sales and the five largest 56%, so one contract loss would move earnings more than any single end-market cycle. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 116; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-17

Margin resilience rests on pass-through pricing, not cost flexibility: metal is 65.51% of 2025 cost of products sold and is passed to customers, yet Adjusted EBITDA over conversion revenue moved from 16.55% in FY2024 to 21.35% in FY2025, 29.58% in nine months 2026 and 19.13% in the third quarter, because metal lag, scrap spreads and plant outages drive much of the swing. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 58–59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-9

Liquidity and the maturity profile are the strongest supports: liquidity of USD 687.2 million is 12.87x trailing cash interest, the revolver is undrawn, and no principal falls due before the revolver matures in October 2030 and the 2031 notes follow, although availability depends on receivable and inventory values that fall with metal prices. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation CALC-12

Capital markets access looks adequate but not cheap: the notes due 2031 and 2034 carry fair values of 91.80% and 93.46% of principal at 2026-09-30, so refinancing at current yields would cost more than the coupons, a matter for 2030 and later rather than now. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation CALC-13

Financial policy is moderate so far: dividends took 20.60% of nine-month 2026 net income, repurchases have been suspended since March 2020 and capital spending is falling, but the incentive plan names no leverage or cash flow measure and the board is led by a combined chairman and chief executive. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-19

Structural and covenant questions are open and bound the view: the guarantor list, the level of the fixed charge coverage test that applies only below an availability threshold, and credit ratings are not supplied, so conclusions rest on reported figures. Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

cells.text: One operating segment selling flat-rolled, extruded and drawn aluminum mill products into four end markets: Aero/HS Products, Packaging, GE Products and Automotive Extrusions
Revenue spreads over aerospace, packaging, general engineering and automotive demand, with packaging the largest by sales
Prices intended to lock in a conversion margin and pass aluminum and certain alloy costs to customers through spot, index-based and firm-price mechanisms
Conversion revenue, not net sales, measures what the business earns; firm-price sales leave metal risk that is hedged with third parties
About 70% of shipments go directly to manufacturers or tier one suppliers and about 30% to metal service centers; largest customer 16% of 2025 net sales; five largest customers 56%
Concentrated revenue: the loss of one large customer would be material
Primary aluminum and scrap bought from third parties; top five primary aluminum suppliers supplied 82% of 2025 primary aluminum pounds and the largest supplier 24%
Supply is concentrated in a few vendors, which raises availability and premium risk
13 principal production facilities with 10,384,000 square feet; Warrick, a dedicated packaging site, is the largest at 3,943,000 square feet; 729,000 square feet are leased
Mostly owned plants, with output concentrated at Warrick, Trentwood and Newark, the three largest sites
3,840 employees at 2025-12-31; about 65% under labor contracts; 26% of those covered by contracts expiring within one year
Contract renewals recur across plants; a stoppage would interrupt shipments
Packaging shipments weighted to the second half of the year; aerospace, general engineering and automotive shipments weighted slightly to the first half
Quarterly cash flow is smoothed across end markets, with planned major maintenance in low-demand periods
Trentwood Phase VII expansion and a fourth coating line at Warrick; capital spending USD 180.8 million in 2024 and USD 136.9 million in 2025; 2026 plan of approximately USD 130.0 million
Capacity has been added at Trentwood and Warrick and the Warrick coating line is still ramping, so capital spending is falling while volume rises
Receivables transferred under customer-based supply chain financing programs equal about 32% of 2025 net sales and 31% of third-quarter 2026 net sales; costs are typically reimbursed by the customer
Cash conversion depends on customer programs that are outside reported debt
Alcoa Corporation supplies resources such as potable water to Warrick; the agreements' terms are not in the supplied pages
A failure by the supplier could shut the largest plant

runs.text: The first strength is liquidity and a clear maturity runway: liquidity of USD 687.2 million, an undrawn revolver and no principal due before October 2030 mean a metal price shock or a customer stoppage would be absorbed before it became a refinancing problem, which supports a low near-term default pathway and gives management room to wait out the cycle. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 31; calculation CALC-12

The second strength is the earnings recovery beyond metal lag: Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag nearly doubled in the nine months of 2026 and net leverage fell by 1.40x, so debt service capacity is stronger than a year ago and trailing cover of 8.73x on cash interest gives wide room, although the run rate is below the trailing figure. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-5

The third strength is pass-through pricing: index and spot pricing pass aluminum and alloy cost to customers, firm-price sales are only 11.43% of shipments, and packaging conversion revenue per pound rose 17.89%, so the business earns on conversion rather than on metal and most price swings do not reach EBITDA, except through lag and scrap spreads. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16

The fourth strength is a qualified position that is hard to enter: suppliers must pass rigorous qualification, some packaging approvals take multiple years, and the company has added capacity at Trentwood and a coating line at Warrick, so the recovery in volume after the 2025 outage has a barrier against new entrants and supports revenue durability. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 64; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The fifth strength is moderate financial policy: repurchases are suspended, dividends are 20.60% of nine-month net income and capital spending is falling toward USD 130.0 million for 2026, so cash is not being diverted from debt service and leverage tolerance appears conservative, though no leverage target is stated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-19

The first weakness is customer concentration: the two largest customers take 31% of net sales and the five largest 56%, so loss or repricing of one contract would remove volume from plants with substantial fixed costs and cut EBITDA faster than any end-market cycle, and no contract terms are supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 116; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-17

The second weakness is exposure to metal price timing and working capital: favorable lag was 16.63% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, payables built by USD 157.2 million, and receivables sold under customer programs rose 33.98%, so a price fall would reverse earnings and cash flow while shrinking the borrowing base that supports liquidity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 29, 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-12

The third weakness is unproven free cash flow: free cash flow was negative in FY2024 and FY2025 and capital spending ran at 1.12x depreciation in FY2025, so the trailing positive figure depends on lower capital spending and a payables build and may not persist at the planned fourth-quarter spending of USD 57.8 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11

The fourth weakness is margin volatility and the third-quarter slowdown: Adjusted EBITDA over conversion revenue fell to 19.13% in the third quarter from 29.58% in the nine months, with scrap spreads, the Bellwood outage and coating line ramp-up named as causes, so the improved margins of 2026 are not yet a stable base. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-8

The fifth weakness is opacity of the creditor position: guarantors, the fixed charge coverage trigger level and ratings are not supplied, a combined chairman and chief executive leads the board, and the incentive plan names no leverage measure, so creditors cannot test structural ranking or covenant headroom. Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Kaiser's only financing transactions in the period were completed in the fourth quarter of 2025. In November 2025 it issued USD 500.0 million of unsecured senior notes due 2034-03-01 at par and redeemed in full the USD 500.0 million of unsecured notes due March 2028 at 100% of principal, funded by the new notes, cash on hand and revolver borrowings; USD 2.1 million of unamortized issuance costs on the old notes was written off. The new notes carry a coupon 1.25 percentage points above the old notes, which adds USD 6.25 million of annual interest on the same amount, and the maturity moves out by 6 years. The company may be required to offer to repurchase the new notes on certain asset sales or on a change of control accompanied by a ratings decline. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 102–103; calculation CALC-15

In October 2025 the asset-based revolver was amended to mature in October 2030 with a maximum commitment of USD 575.0 million, of which up to USD 50.0 million may be used for letters of credit, and an accordion of USD 200.0 million plus a first-in last-out tranche. The amount that can be borrowed is set by eligible receivables, inventory and certain other assets, which secure the revolver. In the nine months of 2026 the company borrowed USD 397.8 million and repaid USD 420.1 million, including the USD 22.3 million drawn at 2025-12-31, and no borrowings were outstanding at 2026-09-30 or 2026-10-19; total liquidity was USD 687.2 million at 2026-09-30. Senior notes principal is USD 1,050.0 million, made up of the 4.50% notes due June 2031 and the notes due 2034. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 31–32; calculation CALC-16

No acquisition, sponsor transaction or business combination is described as occurring in 2024, 2025 or 2026 in the five filings; the filings refer to two earlier acquisitions, Warrick, which closed on 2021-03-31, and Imperial Machine & Tool Co., whose date is not stated. The Sherman, Texas extrusion facility, which was being exited from the second quarter of 2024, was sold in the fourth quarter of 2025 at a charge of USD 7.5 million; sale proceeds are not stated. Quarterly dividends of USD 0.77 per share, about USD 12.8 million each, were declared on 2026-04-13, 2026-07-13 and 2026-10-13, with the last expected to be paid on or about 2026-11-13; payment is not confirmed in any supplied filing. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_kalu-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 88, 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kaiser Aluminum Corp (issuer kalu-811596), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: whether the five supplied filings can support the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work, and what remains missing. The cutoff is 2026-11-18 and the current period is Q3 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No output of another module is an input to this module.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five supplied filings, the latest for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, support the requested credit snapshot of Kaiser Aluminum Corp with limitations, so creditors can rely on reported debt, liquidity and earnings but not on covenant headroom, guarantor coverage or ratings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 14–15, 29, 31; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three limits shape how far the figures can be used. The 2025 annual report adjusts 2024 and 2023 for an inventory accounting change, so the 2024 annual report is not comparable for those years. The quarterly reports do not state the inventory basis of their 2025 comparatives. The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the level of the springing fixed charge coverage test and the list of guarantors are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant terms are not established. No supplied filing prints the level of the springing fixed charge coverage test, the availability level that switches it on, or any indenture covenant level, and the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied. Every filing was searched for fixed charge coverage, availability threshold, financial covenant, springing and ratio-level wording; management says only that it does not expect to trigger the test in the next 12 months. Covenant headroom cannot be calculated and the legal and covenant analysis cannot run.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The guarantors of the Senior Notes are not named. The 2024 annual report says certain subsidiaries are not guarantors of the Senior Notes or the Revolving Credit Facility, the 2025 annual report drops that statement, and neither names the guarantors or prints guarantor and non-guarantor financial information. Only the four revolver borrowers are named, so structural priority and asset coverage by entity cannot be established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating is stated in any filing or in the run settings. Ratings appear only as a factor in financing terms, in the credit thresholds that set derivative collateral for counterparties and in the change-of-control offer to repurchase the 5.875% notes, which applies when the change is accompanied by a ratings decline. Rating-based pricing and triggers cannot be assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2024 annual report and the 2025 annual report give different 2024 amounts because the company changed its inventory valuation method on 2025-01-01. Net income for 2024 is USD 46.8 million in the first and USD 65.7 million as adjusted in the second; Adjusted EBITDA for 2024 is USD 216.5 million in the first and USD 241.0 million as adjusted in the second. Had the former method continued, 2025 would have shown a net loss of USD 29.1 million instead of net income of USD 112.5 million. The 2025 annual report is the later filing and controls FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023; FY2022 exists only in the 2024 annual report on the former method, so any series that reaches back to FY2022 mixes bases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The three 2026 quarterly reports do not say which inventory method their 2025 comparative figures use, and the 2025 quarterly reports are not supplied. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kaiser Aluminum Corp (issuer kalu-811596), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: normalised statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage for FY2023 to FY2025 and the periods to September 30, 2026. The sources are the two annual reports and three 2026 quarterly reports supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Upstream module outputs supplied to this module:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt is 1.98x trailing reported EBITDA at September 30, 2026 and liquidity is USD 687.2 million, so creditors have no near-term refinancing pressure, but the earnings recovery leans on metal price timing and a USD 157.2 million payables build.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 14, 29, 31; calculation CALC-30; calculation CALC-56; calculation CALC-86

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross debt is flat at USD 1,038.7 million of unsecured notes with the revolver undrawn, and net leverage would be 2.00x after the dividend declared on 2026-10-13. The covenant test level is not stated, so headroom cannot be measured, and the 2024 annual report is not comparable with later periods for 2024 and 2023.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ratios use calculated reported EBITDA, not the Adjusted EBITDA the issuer states, and the interim dates use trailing twelve months whose 2025 comparative periods have an inventory basis the quarterly reports do not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cover is measured on cash interest paid, which is below interest expense because part of the expense is capitalized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The revolver is borrowing-base limited, so availability can fall with metal prices even though the commitment is USD 575.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ladder is drawn at 2026-09-30 from instrument maturity dates and is principal, not carrying value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: All three rows are fiscal years and the EBITDA is issuer-adjusted, not the calculated reported EBITDA used in the ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ranking is inferred from the stated security because no filing ranks the notes against the revolver, and amounts are principal, not carrying value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The bridge is for FY2025 and the three adjustments sum exactly to the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events: a quarterly dividend of USD 0.77 per share was declared on 2026-10-13, with about USD 12.8 million expected to be paid on or about 2026-11-13; it is kept out of the period figures and shown in the post-balance-sheet table. The 2025 annual report states that revolver borrowings of USD 62.4 million, including USD 40.1 million drawn after year end, were repaid by 2026-02-16; that sits inside the 2026 interim figures and does not change 2026-09-30 net debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The KPI sources are the end-market and Conversion Revenue tables of the 2025 annual report and the third-quarter report, the Adjusted EBITDA notes and the supply chain financing notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt fell from USD 1,052.6 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 921.4 million at 2026-09-30 while trailing reported EBITDA rose from USD 311.3 million to USD 466.1 million, so net leverage dropped from 3.38x to 1.98x. About 1.12x of that fall comes from higher EBITDA and 0.28x from lower net debt, which is cash build rather than repayment because gross debt moved only from USD 1,059.6 million to USD 1,038.7 million. Cash interest paid over the trailing twelve months is USD 53.4 million, which gives cover of 8.73x, up from 6.21x in FY2025 and 5.64x in FY2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; calculation CALC-87; calculation CALC-91; calculation CALC-88; calculation CALC-89; calculation CALC-90

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that earnings include favorable metal price lag of about USD 63.0 million in the first nine months of 2026 and USD 93.0 million in FY2025, which is 16.63% and 29.98% of issuer Adjusted EBITDA. Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was only USD 2.7 million above the prior year and the lag turned unfavorable by about USD 1.0 million, and the issuer now expects full-year Adjusted EBITDA growth toward the lower end of its range. A fall in metal prices would reverse the lag benefit and shrink borrowing-base availability at the same time. Without the trailing twelve months metal price lag of about USD 92.0 million, trailing reported EBITDA would be USD 374.1 million and net leverage 2.46x rather than 1.98x; that is the level the figures support if the lag is treated as non-recurring.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation CALC-71; calculation CALC-72; calculation CALC-73; calculation CALC-94; calculation CALC-95; calculation CALC-96

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow for nine months 2026 is USD 248.1 million against USD 132.0 million a year earlier, but USD 157.2 million of it is a payables increase from higher metal costs and payment timing, set against inventory and receivables builds of USD 123.4 million and USD 108.4 million. Capital expenditure fell to USD 72.2 million from USD 106.4 million, so free cash flow reached USD 175.9 million against USD 25.6 million; on a trailing basis it is USD 124.8 million, after negative free cash flow of USD 25.5 million in FY2025. Dividends of USD 39.2 million were paid in nine months 2026. The issuer's plan of about USD 130.0 million of capital spending for 2026 implies about USD 57.8 million in the fourth quarter against an average of USD 24.07 million a quarter in the first nine months, so nine-month free cash flow overstates the run rate. The payables build is a timing benefit that reverses if metal prices fall or suppliers shorten terms, which would take cash back out of liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 32; calculation CALC-69; calculation CALC-68; calculation CALC-70; calculation CALC-67; calculation CALC-92; calculation CALC-93

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is USD 687.2 million: cash of USD 117.3 million plus USD 569.9 million of revolver availability after USD 5.1 million of letters of credit, up from USD 547.2 million at 2025-12-31. Restricted cash of USD 19.6 million is excluded. The revolver commitment of USD 575.0 million is undrawn and matures in October 2030, the 4.50% notes of USD 550.0 million fall due in June 2031 and the 5.875% notes of USD 500.0 million in March 2034, so no principal is due before 2030. The revolver is limited by a borrowing base of eligible receivables and inventory, so availability depends on metal prices and working capital.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 19, 31; calculation CALC-35; calculation CALC-40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2025 annual report applied the change from last-in, first-out to weighted average cost inventory retrospectively, so FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA is USD 241.0 million there and USD 216.5 million in the 2024 annual report, a difference of USD 24.5 million; the 2025 annual report amounts are used, and FY2022 is not comparable. Reported EBITDA is calculated because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA, and the two differ by only USD 1.1 million in FY2025. Receivables sold under customer supply chain financing were USD 991.6 million in nine months 2026, are derecognized and sit outside the reported debt, and the issuer's own percentage of sales cannot be rebuilt from the amounts printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: covenant headroom is not calculable. No supplied filing prints the level of the springing fixed charge coverage test or the availability that switches it on, and the credit agreement is not supplied; management states only that it does not expect to trigger the test in the next 12 months. Obtaining the credit agreement would close this.

fields.name: Quote

The 2025 annual report is used. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kaiser Aluminum Corp (issuer kalu-811596), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: business, ownership, governance, transaction and corporate-structure facts from the five supplied filings, covering 2024 to the quarter ended 2026-09-30. No acquisition or sponsor transaction is supplied; the transactions covered are the 2025 refinancing, the revolver amendment and one asset exit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Upstream module outputs supplied to this module:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kaiser is a listed, single-segment maker of specialty aluminum mill products with no controlling owner disclosed, so creditors rely on operating cash flow and board discipline, not on sponsor support. The only recent financing transactions were an amount-neutral refinancing of the 2028 notes into notes due 2034 and a revolver extension to October 2030, which pushed maturities out but raised the coupon on the refinanced amount by 1.25 percentage points.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Holder-level ownership, board independence and guarantor coverage are not established because the proxy statement and the indentures are not supplied, so the ranking of the notes against subsidiary creditors cannot be assessed here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Conversion revenue is a better gauge of the business than net sales: net sales rose 46.40% in the nine months of 2026 while conversion revenue, the part left after metal cost, rose 17.68%, so most of the growth is metal pass-through that enlarges receivables and inventory rather than margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Packaging is the largest line by sales but contributes less to margin than its sales share suggests: it is 45.84% of nine-month 2026 net sales and 39.95% of conversion revenue, while aerospace plate is 24.71% of net sales and 31.00% of conversion revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 30; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration is the main business risk: the two largest customers took 31% of 2025 net sales and the five largest 56%, and the annual report says losing the largest could have a material adverse effect.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Metal-price neutrality is substantial but incomplete: firm-price sales exposed the company on 11.43% of 2025 shipments by weight, and alloy cost pass-through can lag, so earnings still swing with metal timing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer supply chain financing makes cash conversion depend on customers: receivables transferred under customer programs equalled 32% of 2025 net sales and 31% of third-quarter 2026 net sales, and they sit outside reported debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling holder appears in the evidence supplied, which lowers event risk from a financial sponsor, though holder concentration is untested: the stock is listed on Nasdaq and a classified board is led by a combined chairman and chief executive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Distributions are steady and moderate against earnings, but cash cover is not yet proven: operating cash flow covered capital spending plus dividends only 0.59x in 2025, and the 2.23x cover in the nine months of 2026 was helped by a USD 157.2 million build in accounts payable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditor access to subsidiary assets is not established: the company is a holding company over wholly owned operating subsidiaries, four of which are revolver borrowers, the notes carry guarantors named only in the indentures, and the warning in the 2024 annual report that certain subsidiaries are not guarantors is absent from later reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Labor exposure is concentrated near the as-of date: about 65% of employees are unionized, the Richmond contracts expire in November 2026, and the 2026 quarterly reports are silent on the earlier 2026 renewals, while the Trentwood and Newark contracts run to September 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Warrick, the largest plant by floor area, is a single point of dependence: it is the dedicated packaging site and relies on Alcoa for essential resources such as potable water, under agreements whose terms are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a benign ownership and event-risk reading is what the filings leave out: holder-level ownership, the party to a director designation agreement that appears in the exhibit lists with dates of 2021 and April 2025, and the guarantor list. A holder with board designation rights, or a large holder pressing for distributions, would raise event risk, and a debt-funded buyback or acquisition would change the view; the USD 93.1 million repurchase authorization has been unused since March 2020 but remains available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest operating counterpoint is that the 2026 recovery is real but partly metal-driven: shipments rose 7.94% and conversion revenue per pound rose, yet net sales grew far faster than conversion revenue, so a fall in metal prices would reverse part of the working capital build. Loss of one of the two largest customers, which hold 31% of net sales, or a stoppage at Richmond or another plant would also weaken the view. Confirmation would come from a proxy statement showing dispersed holders, indentures showing that all material operating subsidiaries guarantee the notes, and renewal of the Richmond contracts without disruption.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 30; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The no-sponsor reading rests on cover-page share counts and the number of record holders; beneficial-owner percentages, director independence and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a single large holder would overturn it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The statement that creditors may rank behind subsidiary creditors rests on one risk-factor paragraph in the 2024 annual report, because the guarantor lists are named only in documents not supplied; full guarantee coverage would remove this concern.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer shares are as printed for 2025 only; contract terms, expiry dates and customer names are not supplied, so the concentration conclusion cannot say how soon revenue is at risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Labor conclusions stop at the contract expiry dates printed at 2025-12-31; renewal outcomes in 2026 are not stated, so the Richmond expiry in November 2026 is shown as unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The dividend declared on 2026-10-13 is shown as scheduled for 2026-11-13 because no filing after 2026-10-22 is supplied, so distributions after the latest report are not confirmed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kaiser's only financing transactions in the period were completed in the fourth quarter of 2025. In November 2025 it issued USD 500.0 million of unsecured senior notes due 2034-03-01 at par and redeemed in full the USD 500.0 million of unsecured notes due March 2028 at 100% of principal, funded by the new notes, cash on hand and revolver borrowings; USD 2.1 million of unamortized issuance costs on the old notes was written off. The new notes carry a coupon 1.25 percentage points above the old notes, which adds USD 6.25 million of annual interest on the same amount, and the maturity moves out by 6 years. The company may be required to offer to repurchase the new notes on certain asset sales or on a change of control accompanied by a ratings decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In October 2025 the asset-based revolver was amended to mature in October 2030 with a maximum commitment of USD 575.0 million, of which up to USD 50.0 million may be used for letters of credit, and an accordion of USD 200.0 million plus a first-in last-out tranche. The amount that can be borrowed is set by eligible receivables, inventory and certain other assets, which secure the revolver. In the nine months of 2026 the company borrowed USD 397.8 million and repaid USD 420.1 million, including the USD 22.3 million drawn at 2025-12-31, and no borrowings were outstanding at 2026-09-30 or 2026-10-19; total liquidity was USD 687.2 million at 2026-09-30. Senior notes principal is USD 1,050.0 million, made up of the 4.50% notes due June 2031 and the notes due 2034.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No acquisition, sponsor transaction or business combination is described as occurring in 2024, 2025 or 2026 in the five filings; the filings refer to two earlier acquisitions, Warrick, which closed on 2021-03-31, and Imperial Machine & Tool Co., whose date is not stated. The Sherman, Texas extrusion facility, which was being exited from the second quarter of 2024, was sold in the fourth quarter of 2025 at a charge of USD 7.5 million; sale proceeds are not stated. Quarterly dividends of USD 0.77 per share, about USD 12.8 million each, were declared on 2026-04-13, 2026-07-13 and 2026-10-13, with the last expected to be paid on or about 2026-11-13; payment is not confirmed in any supplied filing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kaiser Aluminum Corp (issuer kalu-811596), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: the fundamental credit profile built from the five supplied filings and the accepted outputs on source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance, covering the period to 2026-09-30. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or recovery view is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Upstream module outputs supplied to this module:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kaiser's fundamental credit profile is adequate: trailing net leverage of 1.98x (2.00x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-10-13) and no maturity before October 2030 limit near-term refinancing risk, but earnings have slowed since the first half.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 31; calculation CALC-1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was USD 84.0 million against an average of USD 147.4 million a quarter in the first half, and an outlook at the low end of the issuer's range implies leverage near 2.97x on the second-half run rate. Customer concentration, metal price timing and covenant and guarantor terms that are not supplied keep the view at adequate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 31; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deleveraging is real and mostly earnings-driven: net debt of USD 921.4 million (USD 934.2 million pro forma for the dividend) is 1.98x trailing EBITDA (2.00x pro forma) against 3.38x at 2025-12-31, a fall of 1.40x of which 1.12x came from higher EBITDA and only 0.28x from lower net debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Underlying earnings improved by more than the metal price lag explains: Adjusted EBITDA excluding the favorable lag was USD 315.8 million in the nine months of 2026 against USD 158.4 million a year earlier, and the lag's share of Adjusted EBITDA fell from 28.78% to 16.63%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Momentum is slowing and the trailing figures flatter the run rate: Adjusted EBITDA fell from an average of USD 147.4 million a quarter in the first half to USD 84.0 million in the third quarter, and the outlook, which the issuer now places toward the low end of 45% to 55% growth, implies about USD 70.99 million in the fourth quarter if it lands at 45%, which puts leverage at 2.97x on the second-half run rate before the dividend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 31; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is the least proven dimension: it was USD -13.7 million in FY2024 and USD -25.5 million in FY2025 and reached USD 124.8 million on a trailing basis only after capital spending fell and USD 157.2 million of payables built, so cash conversion has not been shown through a metal price cycle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is moderate and customer-led: packaging is 39.95% and aerospace plate 31.00% of nine-month 2026 conversion revenue, but the two largest customers take 31% of net sales and the five largest 56%, so one contract loss would move earnings more than any single end-market cycle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 116; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin resilience rests on pass-through pricing, not cost flexibility: metal is 65.51% of 2025 cost of products sold and is passed to customers, yet Adjusted EBITDA over conversion revenue moved from 16.55% in FY2024 to 21.35% in FY2025, 29.58% in nine months 2026 and 19.13% in the third quarter, because metal lag, scrap spreads and plant outages drive much of the swing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 58–59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the maturity profile are the strongest supports: liquidity of USD 687.2 million is 12.87x trailing cash interest, the revolver is undrawn, and no principal falls due before the revolver matures in October 2030 and the 2031 notes follow, although availability depends on receivable and inventory values that fall with metal prices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital markets access looks adequate but not cheap: the notes due 2031 and 2034 carry fair values of 91.80% and 93.46% of principal at 2026-09-30, so refinancing at current yields would cost more than the coupons, a matter for 2030 and later rather than now.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is moderate so far: dividends took 20.60% of nine-month 2026 net income, repurchases have been suspended since March 2020 and capital spending is falling, but the incentive plan names no leverage or cash flow measure and the board is led by a combined chairman and chief executive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Structural and covenant questions are open and bound the view: the guarantor list, the level of the fixed charge coverage test that applies only below an availability threshold, and credit ratings are not supplied, so conclusions rest on reported figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate profile is the earnings run rate: the first half of 2026 carried most of the improvement, third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA grew only 3.32% on net sales growth of 43.98%, and an annualised second half at the low end of the issuer's outlook leaves net debt of USD 921.4 million (USD 934.2 million pro forma for the dividend) at 2.97x, close to 2.96x if EBITDA simply returned to its 2025 level. The nine-month cash flow is also flattered by USD 157.2 million of payables, and a fall in aluminum prices would reverse that build and lower the borrowing base at the same moment, taking liquidity to USD 530.0 million before any base reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest counter-argument is that the earnings improvement is not merely metal: excluding the lag, third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was 59.47% higher and its margin on conversion revenue rose to 19.36% from 15.20%, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose 17.89%, and capital spending is falling. The view would improve with full-year 2026 free cash flow that stays positive after the payables build unwinds, a fourth quarter near the high end of the outlook, and disclosure that the covenant test is far from its trigger and that guarantors cover the operating subsidiaries. It would weaken with a fourth quarter at or below the low end, loss of one of the two largest customers, a metal price fall that cuts the borrowing base, or a stoppage at the Richmond plant.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–31; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-7; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The leverage conclusion uses trailing figures built from the 2025 annual report and quarterly comparatives whose inventory basis is not stated, so a different basis for the 2025 quarters would move trailing EBITDA and leverage by an amount that cannot be measured here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The run-rate range of 2.48x to 2.97x rests on the issuer's own outlook for 2026, which is a range and an opinion; no order book, customer volume schedule or monthly result is supplied to test it, so it could prove wrong in either direction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The liquidity and refinancing view stops at reported ratios because the fixed charge coverage trigger level, the borrowing base cushion above the USD 575.0 million commitment and the covenant package are not supplied; tighter terms would lower the liquidity assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The adequate rating of the profile is judged against the issuer's own history, not against peers, because no peer data, agency ratings or market spreads are supplied; a peer comparison could move it either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The reading of the notes' ranking against subsidiary creditors is excluded from this view, so a fuller opinion on loss severity would need guarantor coverage that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is liquidity and a clear maturity runway: liquidity of USD 687.2 million, an undrawn revolver and no principal due before October 2030 mean a metal price shock or a customer stoppage would be absorbed before it became a refinancing problem, which supports a low near-term default pathway and gives management room to wait out the cycle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is the earnings recovery beyond metal lag: Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag nearly doubled in the nine months of 2026 and net leverage fell by 1.40x, so debt service capacity is stronger than a year ago and trailing cover of 8.73x on cash interest gives wide room, although the run rate is below the trailing figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is pass-through pricing: index and spot pricing pass aluminum and alloy cost to customers, firm-price sales are only 11.43% of shipments, and packaging conversion revenue per pound rose 17.89%, so the business earns on conversion rather than on metal and most price swings do not reach EBITDA, except through lag and scrap spreads.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth strength is a qualified position that is hard to enter: suppliers must pass rigorous qualification, some packaging approvals take multiple years, and the company has added capacity at Trentwood and a coating line at Warrick, so the recovery in volume after the 2025 outage has a barrier against new entrants and supports revenue durability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth strength is moderate financial policy: repurchases are suspended, dividends are 20.60% of nine-month net income and capital spending is falling toward USD 130.0 million for 2026, so cash is not being diverted from debt service and leverage tolerance appears conservative, though no leverage target is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is customer concentration: the two largest customers take 31% of net sales and the five largest 56%, so loss or repricing of one contract would remove volume from plants with substantial fixed costs and cut EBITDA faster than any end-market cycle, and no contract terms are supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 116; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is exposure to metal price timing and working capital: favorable lag was 16.63% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, payables built by USD 157.2 million, and receivables sold under customer programs rose 33.98%, so a price fall would reverse earnings and cash flow while shrinking the borrowing base that supports liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 29, 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is unproven free cash flow: free cash flow was negative in FY2024 and FY2025 and capital spending ran at 1.12x depreciation in FY2025, so the trailing positive figure depends on lower capital spending and a payables build and may not persist at the planned fourth-quarter spending of USD 57.8 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is margin volatility and the third-quarter slowdown: Adjusted EBITDA over conversion revenue fell to 19.13% in the third quarter from 29.58% in the nine months, with scrap spreads, the Bellwood outage and coating line ramp-up named as causes, so the improved margins of 2026 are not yet a stable base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is opacity of the creditor position: guarantors, the fixed charge coverage trigger level and ratings are not supplied, a combined chairman and chief executive leads the board, and the incentive plan names no leverage measure, so creditors cannot test structural ranking or covenant headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kaiser is a single-segment producer of semi-fabricated specialty aluminum mill products, and its revenue splits over four cyclical end markets in which packaging is the largest by sales and aerospace plate the second-largest contributor to conversion revenue. About 70% of shipments go directly to manufacturers and tier one suppliers, mostly under long-term agreements with metal pass-through pricing, so volume is reasonably visible while margin visibility depends on a few large contracts and on metal timing; debt service capacity therefore rests on conversion revenue, not on net sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 16; calculation CALC-14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kaiser is a Nasdaq-listed holding company with no sponsor or controlling holder stated, operating through wholly owned subsidiaries of which four borrow under the revolver; holder-level ownership and the guarantor list are not supplied. The board is classified and chaired by the chief executive, and the incentive plan rewards total shareholder return and Adjusted EBITDA margin, so financial discipline rests on policy choices already visible: repurchases suspended since March 2020 and dividends at 20.60% of nine-month net income.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 35; calculation CALC-19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Volume and mix, not price, drive earned revenue: shipments rose 7.94% in the nine months of 2026 and conversion revenue per pound rose to USD 1.42 from USD 1.30, while net sales grew 46.40% on metal pass-through and conversion revenue only 17.68%. Firm-price sales are 11.43% of 2025 shipments, so pricing power shows in conversion margin rather than in net sales, and packaging conversion revenue per pound rose 17.89% as coated products ramped. Demand is cyclical in aerospace and automotive, concentrated in a few customers and exposed to substitution by composites, steel and plastics, according to the risk factors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 26–27; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Metal is 65.51% of 2025 cost of products sold and passes through to customers, leaving non-metal costs of USD 1,010.8 million (34.49%) made up of manufacturing 23.70%, plant overhead 6.19%, freight 2.87% and other 1.73%, with a high share of fixed cost in packaging that makes margin depend on plant utilization. Operating leverage cut both ways: in 2025 lower volume and start-up costs were outweighed by favorable metal consumption cost and mix, and in the third quarter of 2026 net sales grew 43.98% but Adjusted EBITDA only 3.32% because of lower scrap utilization, tighter scrap spreads, planned outages and freight, so margins can be defended against metal but not against operating deleverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 56, 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA has converted weakly into free cash flow: capital spending was 9.42% of conversion revenue and 1.12x depreciation in FY2025, free cash flow was -5.99% and -8.19% of reported EBITDA in FY2024 and FY2025, and the trailing 26.78% follows lower capital spending and a net working capital outflow of USD 74.6 million that is helped by the payables build. Capital spending is discretionary and the plan of USD 130.0 million implies USD 57.8 million in the fourth quarter, so flexibility exists if volumes weaken; leases, pension and retiree obligations and the environmental accrual sit outside debt but are small beside it, according to Financial foundation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 34; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate and tied to scale: some competitors for aerospace plate and packaging are substantially larger, and imports and trade orders can alter pricing, so margin cannot be assumed to hold in a downturn. New entrants face multi-year customer qualification and heavy equipment investment, which protects volume, although the filing warns that new parties may qualify. Substitutes matter by end market, with composites and titanium in aircraft, steel in vehicles and glass or plastic in packaging, and a high aluminum price can push customers to switch. Buyer power is the largest force because five customers take 56% of net sales, though long-term agreements and index pricing soften it. Supplier power is moderate: five suppliers provide 82% of primary aluminum and Warrick depends on one party for essential resources, so a supply failure would hit output more than margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trade policy is material to credit because the filing lists duties and tariffs among the drivers of primary aluminum pricing, and the Midwest premium rose from USD 0.19 to USD 0.59 per pound, which with the LME price lifted the average to USD 1.78 in 2025 from USD 1.29 in 2024, up 37.98%; that inflates receivables, inventory and the borrowing base on the way up and reverses on the way down. Fuel-efficiency standards and defense budgets move aerospace and automotive demand, and sustainability preferences support aluminum packaging, but the filings give no quantified effect, so these are monitored rather than weighted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit strengths are liquidity with a long maturity runway, earnings recovery beyond metal lag, pass-through pricing, qualification barriers and moderate financial policy; the weaknesses are customer concentration, metal and working capital timing, unproven free cash flow, margin volatility and an opaque creditor position. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the coated packaging ramp, aerospace plate volume on the added Trentwood capacity and lower capital spending; threats are a metal price fall that shrinks the borrowing base, a customer loss, a plant stoppage and refinancing at higher yields after 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The nine dimensions assess as follows. Scale and market position is average, with USD 3,373.0 million of 2025 net sales but larger competitors. Competitive advantage is average, resting on qualification barriers and coated packaging capability. Business diversification is average because four end markets are offset by customer concentration. Cost and capex flexibility is average, since metal passes through and capital spending is discretionary but fixed costs are high in packaging. Margin stability is weak, with the margin on conversion revenue ranging from 16.55% to 29.58% across comparable periods. Free cash flow stability is weak, with negative free cash flow in FY2024 and FY2025. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average, with no maturity before October 2030 but notes valued below principal. Liquidity position is strong at USD 687.2 million, subject to the borrowing base. Financial policy and governance is average, with moderate distributions offset by open structural and covenant terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 31; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For the next 12 to 24 months the issuer expects conversion revenue growth toward the high end of 10% to 15% and Adjusted EBITDA growth toward the low end of 45% to 55%, which implies a fourth quarter below the third because of planned outages, execution, customer year-end inventory alignment and metal headwinds, while the coated packaging ramp, aerospace plate volume and lower capital spending are tailwinds and weaker automotive extrusion volume is a headwind. Over three to five years the maturity profile is benign until the revolver in October 2030 and the notes in 2031 and 2034, and refinancing cost will depend on yields that currently value the notes below principal; management's longer-term demand view is stated in its own words and is not tested here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 31; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a fall in aluminum prices together with customer destocking in aerospace and automotive. The first operational break is metal price lag turning unfavorable and scrap spreads staying tight, which cuts Adjusted EBITDA toward the 2025 level and puts net debt of USD 921.4 million (USD 934.2 million pro forma for the dividend) at 2.96x, or 4.03x at the 2024 level. The financial transmission is a reversal of the USD 157.2 million payables build and falling receivable and inventory values, which lowers the borrowing base and takes liquidity from USD 687.2 million to USD 530.0 million before any base reduction; trailing cover would still be 5.83x at the 2025 EBITDA level. Management can cut capital spending below the USD 130.0 million plan, suspend the dividend of about USD 12.8 million a quarter and draw the undrawn revolver, and no principal is due before October 2030, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress. The first observable signals would be fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA below USD 70.99 million, a fall in the Midwest Transaction Price and renewed revolver borrowing. Primary downside path: a metal price fall that reverses working capital and shrinks the borrowing base while earnings return to the 2025 level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Kaiser presents an adequate business profile supported by liquidity, a long maturity runway, pass-through pricing and a recovery in underlying earnings, but credit quality is constrained by customer concentration, metal and working capital timing, unproven free cash flow and slowing quarterly earnings. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because trailing free cash flow of USD 124.8 million rests on lower capital spending and a payables build. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on aluminum prices through the borrowing base, on the cost of refinancing the 2031 and 2034 notes and on covenant terms not supplied. The primary downside path is a metal price fall with customer destocking that reverses working capital and returns earnings to the 2025 level, which would raise net leverage to 2.96x while liquidity stays ample. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the indentures, the proxy statement, peer data and the fourth-quarter result. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: metal price timing and customer concentration.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-12
